clauses.reason: Provision of the order that finds the policies and actions of the Government of Nicaragua an unusual and extraordinary threat and declares a national emergency to deal with that threat. Executive Order No. 12707 of March 13, 1990 finds that the February 25, 1990 election in Nicaragua ended the threat, revokes Executive Order No. 12513 and terminates the national emergency declared in it, and states that it takes effect immediately, so this provision ended on 1990-03-13, the date of that order. The revocation reaches the whole order, so it ends this provision without a separate partial reading. No earlier end is held for this provision.

conflict_resolutions.FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT: The machine read Executive Order No. 12707 as both a whole and a partial ending because of its second sentence preserving actions taken before the effective date. That paragraph is a savings clause that limits the effect of the termination of the emergency on accrued matters; the operative sentence revokes Executive Order No. 12513 in full, so the ending is whole and the savings are recorded separately.

research_rationale:
Identity confirmed against the census register (executive order of 1985-05-01 prohibiting trade and certain other transactions involving Nicaragua) and the held Federal Register text at 50 FR 18629, whose first page is the order. The six paragraphs of the order are all ended together by Executive Order No. 12707 of March 13, 1990, which revokes it and terminates the national emergency; the order takes effect immediately. The held text of Executive Order No. 12707 is the Federal Register text. The later order treats the emergency as still in existence on March 13, 1990, and this claim does not rely on any annual continuation notice, none of which is held.

savings.reason: Section 202 of the National Emergencies Act as applied by Executive Order No. 12707 saves actions taken, proceedings pending, and rights, duties and penalties matured or incurred before the effective date of the termination; those are accrued, and nothing continues the prohibitions after March 13, 1990.
